title: NVIDIA Commits $1 Billion to Advance US Science Over the Next Five Years
key_facts: NVIDIA announced commitments valued at $1 billion over five years to build US capacity for what it calls "super intelligence" research in fields including quantum computing, healthcare and energy security.
The announcement came at the "Science: A New Golden Age" event in Washington, D.C., linked to the Genesis Mission, the US government's AI-for-science programme.
The money is to support higher-education research institutions, US quantum leadership investments and cloud providers serving US government needs.
NVIDIA collaborates on several Genesis Mission phase 2 awards announced the same day, in quantum computing, fusion, accelerator design and microelectronics.
NVIDIA has worked with US national labs for more than two decades, including building the Energy Department's largest science supercomputer at Argonne National Laboratory.
quote_evidence: NVIDIA today announced commitments valued at $1 billion to build out the United States' capacity for super intelligence research and development in fields critical for U.S. leadership, including quantum computing, healthcare and energy security.
NVIDIA is also a collaborator on a number of the phase 2 Genesis Mission awards announced today at the event, including projects in quantum computing, fusion, accelerator design and microelectronics.
why_it_matters_hint: A leading chip maker is promising money and computing support to US research, including quantum.
notes: Company press release; includes standard forward-looking-statement text. No breakdown of how much is new money.
